FCTR – Foreign currency translation reserve. The FCTR arises from the consolidation of the foreign owned subsidiary, Heritage Insurance Tanzania Limited. It represents gains and
losses, including the differences arising as a result of translating opening shareholders’ equity using exchange rates at the end of the reporting period rather than exchange rates
at the beginning of the period which are included in a translation reserve account and reported as a separate component of equity.

The statutory reserve comprises the undistributed life surplus and a separate reserve set aside as required by insurance regulations in Tanzania. Tanzania regulations require
a separate reserve equal to 5% of net written premium or 20% of the net profits whichever is higher. This reserve is capped at minimum paid-up capital or 50% of net written
premiums. Distribution of Liberty Life Kenya surplus to the benefit of the shareholders is on the recommendations of the statutory actuary and is capped to 30% of available
surplus as required by Insurance Act Kenya.

Owner-occupied properties – prior to adoption of IFRS 17, this reserve related to portion of the building properties occupied by the group companies. The reserve previously represented
cumulative gains on revaluations on owner-occupied properties under the previous accounting policies. On adoption of IFRS 17, the group elected to measure owner occupied
properties at fair value through profit or loss as permitted by IAS 16. The reserve was consequently reclassified to retained surplus on the IFRS 17 transition date.
Refer note 39 'Restatement of prior year comparatives' for more detail.
